input: Eurostat release: the euro area unemployment rate was 6.2% in April 2025.

claim.statement: The euro area unemployment rate was 6.2% in April 2025.

analysis.method: Queried Eurostat API for seasonally adjusted monthly unemployment rate (ei_lmhr_m) for April 2025 across all geos, then selected the current euro area aggregate (EA21).
analysis.notes: The seasonally adjusted value for 'Euro area – 21 countries (from 2026)' is 6.3%, not the claimed 6.2%. The claim likely refers to the unadjusted value of 6.2% for the same euro area aggregate.
analysis.script:
import urllib.request, json

url = "https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/api/dissemination/statistics/1.0/data/ei_lmhr_m?format=JSON&lang=EN&indic=LM-UN-T-TOT&s_adj=SA&time=2025-04"
req = urllib.request.Request(url)
with urllib.request.urlopen(req) as resp:
    data = json.loads(resp.read().decode())

dim_ids = data['id']
# The index is a flat index into a multi-dimensional array
# size: [1,1,1,1,46,1] so only geo varies (46 geos)
# index = geo_index (0..45)
geo_cats = data['dimension']['geo']['category']['label']
geo_idx_map = data['dimension']['geo']['category']['index']

# Build reverse map: geo_name -> geo_index
for geo_code, geo_name in sorted(geo_cats.items(), key=lambda x: int(geo_idx_map[x[0]])):
    idx = int(geo_idx_map[geo_code])
    val_key = str(idx)
    val = data['value'].get(val_key, 'N/A')
    if 'Euro area' in geo_name:
        print(f"idx={idx}, geo={geo_name}, val={val}")
        print(f"RESULT {val}")
